laws.fullDescription: Kenya led a Multinational Security Support Mission to Haiti in 2024-25 following UN authorization, deploying police and security forces to combat gang violence that controlled much of the country. Kenya's leadership of an African-led international security mission in the Caribbean was unprecedented.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties for peacekeeping; operational legal framework
exceptions: Status of forces agreement with Haiti
UN authorization framework

quiz.q: What unprecedented international role did Kenya take on in 2024?
options: Leading the multinational security mission to Haiti
quiz.explanation: Kenya led an unprecedented African-led multinational security mission to Haiti in 2024, deploying forces to combat the gang violence that controlled much of the country.

laws.title: M-Pesa Evolution and Fintech Ecosystem
laws.subtitle: Kenya's Mobile Money Transforms East African Finance
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's M-Pesa, the world's most successful mobile money platform, continued evolving with new features including micro-loans, insurance, savings products, and regional expansion. The ecosystem spawned a vibrant fintech startup scene in Nairobi's Silicon Savannah. The Central Bank of Kenya actively regulated the growing sector.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed payment services fines; consumer protection enforcement
exceptions: Mobile money agent licensing
Microinsurance lighter-touch regulation

quiz.q: What is M-Pesa's significance in global financial inclusion?
options: World's most successful mobile money platform
quiz.explanation: M-Pesa is widely considered the world's most successful mobile money platform, pioneering mobile financial services and becoming a global model for financial inclusion.

laws.title: Green Economy and Geothermal Energy Leadership
laws.subtitle: Kenya Runs on Near 100% Renewable Electricity
laws.fullDescription: Kenya achieved near 100% renewable electricity generation primarily through geothermal, hydropower, and wind. The country became an African model for clean energy transition. The geothermal fields in the Rift Valley provided baseload renewable power, and Kenya exported clean energy expertise globally.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; energy regulatory compliance
exceptions: Grid stability requirements
Emergency backup provisions

quiz.q: What source provides Kenya's primary renewable baseload electricity?
quiz.explanation: Kenya's primary renewable baseload electricity comes from geothermal energy extracted from the East African Rift Valley, supplemented by hydro and wind power.

laws.title: Nairobi Silicon Savannah and Tech Hub
laws.subtitle: Kenya Leads Africa in Tech Startup Ecosystem
laws.fullDescription: Nairobi's Silicon Savannah maintained its position as Africa's leading tech startup hub, with companies like Safaricom, M-Kopa, Twiga Foods, and numerous fintech startups attracting international investment. The Konza Technopolis outside Nairobi aimed to create a purpose-built tech city. Kenya produced the most tech unicorns in sub-Saharan Africa.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; data protection and tech regulatory compliance
exceptions: Data localisation requirements
Fintech regulatory sandbox

quiz.q: What is Kenya's tech hub scene nicknamed?
quiz.explanation: Nairobi's thriving tech ecosystem is nicknamed Silicon Savannah, a play on Silicon Valley, reflecting Kenya's status as Africa's leading tech startup hub.

laws.title: M-Pesa Financial Revolution and Digital Economy Leadership
laws.subtitle: Kenya's mobile money system transforms African financial inclusion
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's M-Pesa mobile money platform, launched by Safaricom in 2007, revolutionized financial inclusion across Africa. Over 50 million Kenyans use mobile money, with M-Pesa processing more transactions daily than Western Union globally. Kenya leveraged this into a broader fintech ecosystem with Nairobi becoming Africa's 'Silicon Savannah.' The government promotes Kenya as a regional tech hub, attracting Google, Microsoft, and global startups. Kenya also leads Africa in geothermal energy, generating 51% of electricity from renewables.
laws.penalty: Mobile money operators must maintain KYC compliance and transaction limits for AML purposes
exceptions: Small transactions under $10 have reduced KYC requirements to maintain financial inclusion
Humanitarian cash transfers exempt from standard documentation requirements

laws.title: Gen Z Revolution and Finance Bill Protests
laws.subtitle: Kenya's youth protests overturn government finance bill and shake Ruto
laws.fullDescription: In June 2024, Kenyan Gen Z protesters — organized primarily through TikTok and social media — stormed parliament over a finance bill containing new taxes. At least 39 protesters were killed. The unprecedented youth-led movement forced President Ruto to withdraw the finance bill entirely and eventually dismiss his entire cabinet. The protests demonstrated how social media enables rapid youth political mobilization. Kenya's economic difficulties including high debt, IMF austerity requirements, and cost of living pressures drove the discontent.
laws.penalty: Police use of live ammunition against protesters triggered international condemnation and investigations
exceptions: Peaceful protest rights protected under Kenyan constitution and international law
Social media used to organize protests cannot be restricted without court order

laws.title: Green Bond Market and Climate Finance Leadership
laws.subtitle: Kenya issues Africa's first sovereign green bond
laws.fullDescription: Kenya issued Africa's first sovereign green bond in 2019 and is developing a green bond market to finance climate-resilient infrastructure. Kenya's economy includes significant geothermal power (50%+ of electricity), which it exports knowledge about globally. The Rift Valley's geothermal resources power Nairobi. Kenya's green finance framework is cited as a model for developing countries accessing climate capital. The country also leads in mobile money innovation (M-Pesa) that enables micro-green investment.
laws.penalty: Green bond proceeds must be tracked and reported against eligible green projects under green bond framework
exceptions: Social-environmental blended bonds have different reporting requirements than pure green bonds
Concessional loans from multilateral development banks have separate accounting from market green bonds

quiz.q: What percentage of Kenya's electricity comes from geothermal power?
quiz.explanation: Kenya generates over 50% of its electricity from geothermal power from the Great Rift Valley — making it one of the world's leading geothermal power users and exporter of geothermal expertise.

laws.title: Tea and Horticulture Export Leadership
laws.subtitle: Kenya's Rift Valley produces world's most sought breakfast teas
laws.fullDescription: Kenya is the world's largest tea exporter by volume and third-largest producer. Kenyan black tea — particularly from Kericho and the Rift Valley highlands — is prized for its bright color and strength, forming the base of most global breakfast blends. The Tea Research Foundation of Kenya develops new varieties. Kenya also exports €1 billion+ in cut flowers and vegetables to Europe. The horticulture sector employs 500,000+ workers, mostly women, in high-precision farming for European supermarkets.
laws.penalty: Tea exporters must meet East African Tea Trade Association auction standards and export health certificates
exceptions: Direct sales to premium buyers under traceability certification have expedited export procedures
Organic tea certification allows access to premium markets with separate audit requirements

quiz.q: What rank does Kenya hold in global tea exports by volume?
quiz.explanation: Kenya is the world's largest tea exporter by volume — its bright Rift Valley teas form the base of most global breakfast blends, while also being the world's third-largest tea producer by volume.

laws.title: Mobile Money Revolution and Fintech Innovation Leadership
laws.subtitle: Kenya's M-Pesa transforming finance across Africa
laws.fullDescription: Kenya pioneered mobile money with M-Pesa, launched by Safaricom in 2007, which became the world's first successful large-scale mobile money system. M-Pesa allows users to store money, send and receive payments, and access financial services through basic mobile phones without requiring a bank account. By dramatically expanding financial inclusion, M-Pesa enabled millions of Kenyans to participate in the formal economy for the first time. Kenya has leveraged this foundation to become Africa's premier fintech hub, with Nairobi hosting hundreds of startups and attracting global tech company investment. The M-Pesa model has been exported to multiple African and Asian countries. Kenya also leads in mobile internet penetration and digital government services. However, Kenya's economy faces challenges: significant public debt (used to fund infrastructure including the Standard Gauge Railway), youth unemployment, and recurring drought driven by climate variability. The government has also faced protests over proposed tax increases in 2024.
laws.penalty: Mobile money fraud carries criminal penalties; Central Bank of Kenya regulates fintech operations
exceptions: Small informal transactions below threshold amounts have reduced reporting requirements

quiz.q: In what year was M-Pesa, the world's first successful large-scale mobile money system, launched in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: M-Pesa was launched by Safaricom in Kenya in 2007, pioneering mobile money and becoming the world's first successful large-scale mobile money system, transforming financial inclusion in Kenya and inspiring similar systems globally.

laws.title: Gen Z Tax Protests and Government Accountability Pressure
laws.subtitle: Kenya's youth-led protests reshaping political accountability
laws.fullDescription: Kenya erupted in significant protests in June 2024, led primarily by Generation Z Kenyans organizing through social media, opposing a Finance Bill that proposed substantial tax increases on basic goods including bread, cooking oil, and diapers. The protests forced President William Ruto to withdraw the Finance Bill and led to the dismissal of most of his cabinet. The movement, dubbed Gen Z protests, demonstrated the potential for social media-organized civic action in Africa. Young Kenyans, facing high unemployment despite relatively good education and tech skills, expressed broader frustration with economic governance and corruption. The protests also included demands for government accountability on spending and public debt. Kenya has significant public debt from infrastructure projects including the Standard Gauge Railway built with Chinese loans. The movement raised questions about how governments respond to social media-organized civic pressure.
laws.penalty: Tax laws carry penalties for non-compliance; protest-related charges were brought against some demonstrators
exceptions: Some industries have tax exemptions under investment promotion frameworks

quiz.q: What triggered Kenya's June 2024 Gen Z protests?
options: A Finance Bill proposing tax increases on basic goods including bread and cooking oil
A corruption scandal involving the president
quiz.explanation: Kenya's Gen Z protests began in opposition to a Finance Bill that proposed substantial tax increases on basic goods including bread, cooking oil, and diapers, ultimately forcing President Ruto to withdraw the bill and dismiss most of his cabinet.

laws.title: Silicon Savannah and Tech Startup Ecosystem
laws.subtitle: Kenya as Africa's leading technology innovation hub
laws.fullDescription: Nairobi's Silicon Savannah has established Kenya as one of Africa's most vibrant technology ecosystems, building on the M-Pesa mobile money foundation. Nairobi hosts venture-backed startups across fintech, healthtech, agritech, and logistics. The iHub, founded in 2010, was one of Africa's first tech hubs. International technology companies including Google (which has an Africa office in Nairobi), IBM, and Microsoft have established African operations there. The Konza Technopolis project — a government-built tech city outside Nairobi — aims to create dedicated infrastructure for the tech sector. Kenya's relatively educated workforce, English language proficiency, and sophisticated mobile money infrastructure give it competitive advantages. Challenges include inadequate electricity supply (though Kenya has significant geothermal power), internet connectivity in rural areas, and competition for talent from global companies offering higher salaries.
laws.penalty: Technology companies face data protection obligations under Kenya's Data Protection Act; fintech companies require Central Bank licensing
exceptions: Some regulatory sandboxes allow innovation testing with lighter regulatory requirements

quiz.q: What nickname has Nairobi earned as Africa's leading technology hub?
quiz.explanation: Nairobi has earned the nickname 'Silicon Savannah' as Africa's leading technology innovation hub, building on M-Pesa's mobile money foundation to develop a vibrant startup ecosystem spanning fintech, healthtech, and agritech.

laws.title: Finance Bill Protests Gen Z Revolution
laws.subtitle: Youth uprising defeats finance bill and reshapes Kenyan politics
laws.fullDescription: Kenyan Generation Z protesters flooded the streets in June 2024, opposing the Finance Bill 2024 that proposed new taxes on basic goods. The protests were remarkable for being organized entirely through social media without traditional political leadership. When protesters stormed parliament, President William Ruto withdrew the finance bill entirely, a stunning capitulation. Ruto then dismissed most of his cabinet and formed a broad-based government. The events showed the power of youth-led digital organizing and shifted Kenya's political landscape significantly.
laws.penalty: Finance bill withdrawn; government committed to fiscal restraint measures instead
exceptions: Constitutional right to protest protected; arrested protesters required release
Social media platforms not restricted despite government criticism of organizing role
laws.sourceLabel: Office of the President of Kenya

quiz.q: What was unusual about the organization of Kenya's 2024 Finance Bill protests?
options: They were led by opposition politicians
They were organized by labor unions
They were organized entirely through social media without traditional political leadership
They were coordinated with international NGOs
quiz.explanation: Kenya's 2024 Gen Z protests were organized entirely through social media without traditional political leadership or party coordination, demonstrating the power of digital organizing and representing a new model of youth political action.

laws.title: Worldcoin Iris Scanning and Data Controversy
laws.subtitle: Kenya suspends biometric crypto project amid privacy concerns
laws.fullDescription: Kenya suspended Worldcoin's iris scanning operations in 2023 after the government raised privacy and data protection concerns about the project that scanned people's irises in exchange for cryptocurrency. Worldcoin, the project of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, attracted long queues in Kenya and other developing countries where people accepted iris scans for WorldCoin tokens. The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner launched an investigation. The project raised profound questions about biometric data collection from vulnerable populations for commercial purposes.
laws.penalty: Data collection without proper privacy impact assessment violates Kenya's Data Protection Act 2019
exceptions: Consent-based data collection permitted but must meet informed consent standards
Government-contracted biometric programs have different authorization
laws.sourceLabel: Kenya Office of the Data Protection Commissioner

quiz.q: Who is the CEO of OpenAI who co-founded the Worldcoin iris scanning project?
quiz.explanation: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI (maker of ChatGPT), co-founded Worldcoin which scans people's irises in exchange for cryptocurrency—attracting long queues in Kenya before the government suspended operations over privacy concerns.

laws.title: Green Finance and Climate Investment Hub
laws.subtitle: Nairobi positions as Africa's climate finance capital
laws.fullDescription: Nairobi has become Africa's emerging hub for climate finance and green investment. The Nairobi International Financial Centre aims to capture capital flows into Africa's green transition. Kenya has significant geothermal, wind and solar resources and hosts regional headquarters of multilateral development banks. The country hosted a major debt relief summit in 2023 addressing African sovereign debt. Kenya's mobile money system M-Pesa serves as infrastructure for green finance innovation including pay-as-you-go solar systems reaching millions.
laws.penalty: Green bond regulations require certification of use of proceeds for environmental projects
exceptions: Development finance institution green lending has simplified compliance
Blended finance structures combining grant and commercial capital have special regulatory framework

quiz.q: What unique energy source does Kenya have significant capacity in that most African countries lack?
quiz.explanation: Kenya has significant geothermal power capacity from the Rift Valley's volcanic geology—an unusual renewable energy source that provides reliable baseload power unlike intermittent solar and wind, making Kenya a renewable energy leader in Africa.

laws.title: Climate Change Act and Green Economy Strategy
laws.subtitle: Africa's Renewable Energy Model
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's 2016 Climate Change Act — Africa's first — established mandatory climate change measures for all government functions, requiring climate mainstreaming across sectors. Kenya targets 100% clean energy by 2030 — already at 90%+ renewable electricity (geothermal, hydro, wind, solar). Kenya's geothermal energy from the Rift Valley is world-class, and Lake Turkana Wind Farm is Africa's largest. Kenya's NDC targets 32% emissions reduction by 2030. Climate impacts include drought threatening pastoralists and changing rainfall patterns affecting coffee and tea agriculture.
laws.penalty: Climate Change Act sanctions; National Environment Tribunal empowered; criminal liability for major damage
exceptions: Pastoralist communities under adapted livestock framework
Small-scale farmers

laws.title: Kenya Universal Health Coverage and Linda Mama
laws.subtitle: Beba Beba and Free Maternity Services
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Universal Health Coverage push includes the Linda Mama program providing free maternity services at government facilities — dramatically increasing facility-based births from 43% to over 60% in regions where implemented. Kenya's Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF, 2023) replaced NHIF and aims for universal coverage. Kenya has achieved remarkable progress controlling HIV — from 9% adult prevalence to under 4%, with Kenya having one of Africa's most successful HIV programs. Kenya also faces a significant mental health gap — less than 1% of the health budget goes to mental health for 6+ million Kenyans estimated to have mental disorders.
laws.penalty: SHIF contributions mandatory for all Kenyans including informal sector; employer liability for non-enrollment
exceptions: Vulnerable populations (elderly, disabled, orphans) covered by government
Community health promoters work under simplified regulatory framework

laws.title: Kenya Employment Act and Hustler Nation
laws.subtitle: Informal Economy and Gig Work
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Employment Act provides comprehensive protections for formal workers, but over 80% of Kenyans work informally. President Ruto's 'Hustler' platform focused on empowering informal and small-scale workers through the Hustler Fund (mobile credit). Kenya's tech-driven gig economy — Uber, Bolt, Glovo — employs hundreds of thousands, with ongoing debates about driver rights. Kenya's flower export industry (Lake Naivasha) employs thousands, mostly women, with documented labor rights concerns. The minimum wage varies by sector and region, with Nairobi higher than other areas.
laws.penalty: Employment Act violations: labor courts; industrial court for collective disputes; informal sector largely self-regulated by social norms
exceptions: Domestic workers under Employment Act but with adapted provisions
Agricultural workers under specific wage orders

laws.title: Competency Based Curriculum
laws.subtitle: Kenya's CBC reform replacing the 8-4-4 system
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Competency Based Curriculum (CBC), launched in 2017, replaced the 8-4-4 system with a 2-6-3-3-3 structure (pre-primary through university). CBC emphasizes skills, creativity, and talent development over rote memorization for exams. The Kenya Certificate of Primary Education (KCPE) was replaced with Grade 6 assessments. Kenya abolished primary school fees in 2003, dramatically boosting enrollment. CBC implementation has been controversial due to resource requirements, parental confusion, and assessment changes.
laws.penalty: Schools not implementing CBC face KNEC (Kenya National Examinations Council) sanctions; private schools must register with Teachers Service Commission standards
exceptions: Special needs students receive individualized CBC adaptations
International schools accredited to follow foreign curricula

quiz.q: What structure does Kenya's CBC (Competency Based Curriculum) use to replace the old 8-4-4 system?
quiz.explanation: Kenya's CBC uses a 2-6-3-3-3 structure: 2 years pre-primary, 6 years primary, 3 years lower secondary, 3 years upper secondary, and 3 years university — replacing the old 8-4-4 system (8 primary, 4 secondary, 4 university).

laws.title: Refugees Act and Dadaab Camp
laws.subtitle: Kenya's hosting of world's largest refugee camps
laws.fullDescription: Kenya hosts the world's largest refugee camps: Dadaab (300,000+ Somali refugees, operating since 1991) and Kakuma (250,000+ primarily South Sudanese and Congolese refugees). Kenya periodically threatens to close Dadaab, most recently in 2021, citing security concerns and costs. Kenya's Refugees Act (2021) reformed policy, allowing refugees to work and travel within Kenya under new movement frameworks. Kenya also manages significant Ethiopian and Rwandan immigration and has become an East African business hub attracting skilled workers.
laws.penalty: Refugees found outside designated areas without permits face detention; camps are periodically sealed during security operations; non-registered asylum seekers face deportation under Kenya's non-encampment policy violations
exceptions: Urban refugees may apply for movement passes to live outside camps
UNHCR-registered refugees receive non-refoulement protections

quiz.q: Kenya's Dadaab refugee camp has been operating since 1991 and primarily hosts refugees from which country?
quiz.explanation: Dadaab, in northeastern Kenya near the Somali border, has primarily hosted Somali refugees since its establishment in 1991 during Somalia's civil war. Despite periodic closure threats, it remains one of the world's largest and longest-operating refugee complexes.

laws.title: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act
laws.subtitle: Kenya's drug enforcement and miraa (khat) legality
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act criminalizes most drugs with strict penalties. Like Ethiopia, Kenya has a complex relationship with miraa (khat) — a significant cash crop in Meru County that provides livelihoods for thousands. Kenya exports miraa to Somalia, UK (until ban), and elsewhere. Kenya faces growing heroin problems in coastal cities (Mombasa), with cheap heroin from sea trade routes. Drug trafficking carries life imprisonment. Kenya has harm reduction programs for injection drug users.
laws.penalty: Drug trafficking: life imprisonment; possession for trafficking: 3-10 years; personal use/possession: up to 5 years; cannabis cultivation: up to 10 years; miraa: legal and exported (a significant cash crop)
exceptions: Miraa (khat) is legal in Kenya and is an important agricultural export
Medical narcotics by licensed practitioners
Harm reduction programs operate with NGO support in coastal cities
laws.sourceLabel: Kenya Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act

quiz.q: Kenya's major miraa (khat) export market in the UK was significantly affected when the UK:
options: Banned khat as a controlled substance in 2014
Required all miraa to have THC testing
Classified miraa as a food product instead of drug
quiz.explanation: The UK banned khat in June 2014, making it a Class C controlled substance. This devastated Kenyan miraa exports to the UK, which had been a major market for Meru County farmers, costing the Kenyan economy an estimated £17 million annually.

laws.title: Section 162 — Imprisonment Up to 14 Years
laws.subtitle: Kenya criminalizes same-sex conduct despite a civil rights movement and regional court rulings
laws.fullDescription: Kenya criminalizes same-sex conduct under Section 162 of the Penal Code with penalties up to 14 years imprisonment. In 2019, the High Court upheld these sections despite a legal challenge. In 2023, Kenya's Supreme Court ruled that the National Gay and Lesbian Human Rights Commission had the right to register as an organization. In 2022, the African Court of Human and Peoples' Rights declared Kenya's laws violated rights, but Kenya challenged the ruling. LGBTQ+ Kenyans face police harassment, extortion, and violence.
laws.penalty: Up to 14 years imprisonment under Section 162 of the Penal Code
exceptions: Supreme Court ruled LGBTQ+ organizations may register, though conduct remains criminalized

quiz.q: Despite Kenya's criminalization of homosexuality, what did the Supreme Court rule in 2023?
options: Ordered parliament to change the law
quiz.explanation: Kenya's Supreme Court ruled in 2023 that the National Gay and Lesbian Human Rights Commission had the right to register as an organization, creating an unusual situation where LGBTQ+ conduct remains criminalized but advocacy organizations have legal standing.

laws.title: Press Freedom With Security Law Threats
laws.subtitle: Kenya has active journalism but security laws create press freedom risks
laws.fullDescription: Kenya has a relatively active press landscape. The constitution (Article 34) protects freedom of the media. Kenya has strong independent television (NTV, Citizen TV), newspapers (Daily Nation, The Standard), and digital media (The Elephant, The Conversation Africa). However, security laws including the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act 2018 and the Kenya Information and Communications Act have been used against journalists. Six leading TV channels were temporarily taken off air during the 2017 election protests. The National Cohesion and Integration Act restricts incitement to ethnic hatred but can be applied broadly. Journalists covering government corruption face harassment.
laws.penalty: Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act used against online journalists; temporary TV shutdowns documented
exceptions: Strong Nairobi press corps with significant operational freedom

quiz.q: What happened to six major Kenyan television channels during the 2017 election protests?
options: They were sold to the government
They were temporarily taken off air
Their licenses were suspended for 1 year
quiz.explanation: Six major Kenyan television channels were temporarily taken off air by the government during the disputed 2017 election and protests — a direct censorship action that drew significant international condemnation and concern about press freedom.

laws.title: Computer Misuse and Cybercrime Act and Data Protection Act
laws.subtitle: Kenya has active digital regulation including a data protection framework and cybercrime law
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act (2018) criminalizes cybercrime including cyber-harassment, publishing false information, and computer fraud. Kenya's Data Protection Act (2019) established the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC). Kenya has been active in fintech and mobile money (M-Pesa) regulation. The Communications Authority of Kenya regulates digital services. Kenya has restricted social media and internet access during elections. Kenya's Supreme Court has addressed digital rights in election-related cases. Kenya's tech sector (Silicon Savannah) is significant, creating sophisticated digital governance needs.
laws.penalty: Cybercrime Act: up to 10 years imprisonment for specified offenses; Data Protection Act: fines and regulatory orders
exceptions: Journalism and research exemptions under Data Protection Act
laws.sourceLabel: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner Kenya

quiz.q: What nickname reflects Kenya's significant technology sector and startup ecosystem?
quiz.explanation: Kenya's thriving tech sector and startup ecosystem is nicknamed 'Silicon Savannah' — a play on Silicon Valley — reflecting Kenya's position as Africa's leading tech hub, home to innovations like M-Pesa mobile money and numerous tech startups.

laws.title: CBK Banking Rules & M-Pesa Mobile Money Regulation
laws.subtitle: Kenya pioneered mobile money and now regulates crypto as capital markets products
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Central Bank (CBK) regulates all banks and, critically, Mobile Network Operator (MNO) -led mobile money services. M-Pesa, operated by Safaricom (owned partly by Vodafone/Vodacom), revolutionized financial services — serving over 51 million customers across Africa. The CBK's National Payment System Regulations govern M-Pesa's agent network, transaction limits, and interoperability requirements. For cryptocurrency, Kenya's Capital Markets Authority (CMA) has been developing a regulatory framework since 2022, treating crypto as capital markets products. Kenya's Finance Act 2023 introduced a 3% Digital Asset Tax on crypto transfer values, including P2P transfers.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed mobile money operation: CBK can revoke Safaricom's license; unauthorized banking: fines up to KES 20 million or 5 years imprisonment; Digital Asset Tax evasion: penalties of 25% of unpaid tax plus interest
exceptions: M-Pesa's KES 1 transaction limit for low-value transfers has fee waivers
Agent banking in rural areas has simplified KYC for small accounts
Government-to-person payments through M-Pesa have modified reporting

quiz.q: What cryptocurrency-related tax did Kenya's Finance Act 2023 introduce on digital asset transfers?
options: 20% capital gains tax on crypto profits
3% Digital Asset Tax on the value of every crypto transfer
10% withholding tax on crypto mining income
quiz.explanation: Kenya's Finance Act 2023 introduced a 3% Digital Asset Tax on the transfer value of digital assets — notably applied to the gross transfer value, not profit — meaning even P2P transfers between individuals incur the tax.

laws.title: KEBS & KEPHIS Food Standards & Kenya's Tea/Coffee Export Safety
laws.subtitle: Kenya's food standards protect its premium tea and coffee exports while addressing local food safety
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's food safety is managed by the Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS) for standards, the Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Service (KEPHIS) for agricultural exports, and county health departments for local food establishments. Kenya is the world's third-largest tea exporter (Kenyan tea through Mombasa Tea Auction sets East African prices) and a significant specialty coffee producer. KEBS enforces food standards and conducts market surveillance. Kenya implemented the Nutritional Labelling Regulation 2019 requiring nutritional information on all pre-packaged food. Kenya has a significant street food and informal 'mama mboga' (market vegetable sellers) sector. Aflatoxin contamination of maize (corn) has been a serious public health issue in Kenya, with multiple outbreaks.
laws.penalty: KEBS standards violations: fines up to KES 4 million and 2 years imprisonment; KEPHIS export violation: export ban; food adulteration causing harm: criminal prosecution; aflatoxin-contaminated maize distribution: confiscation and prosecution
exceptions: Mama mboga (small market vegetable sellers) have informal sector recognition with limited formal KEBS requirements
Traditional fermented beverages for local community consumption have cultural exemptions
Tea estates selling directly to factory gate have simplified KEPHIS requirements

quiz.q: What recurring food safety crisis involving a naturally occurring toxin has caused multiple public health emergencies in Kenya?
options: Cholera from contaminated street food water
Aflatoxin contamination of maize (corn) causing poisoning outbreaks
Mercury contamination from Lake Victoria fish
quiz.explanation: Aflatoxin — a naturally occurring mycotoxin produced by Aspergillus mold in maize stored in warm, humid conditions — has caused multiple serious public health outbreaks in Kenya. The 2004 outbreak was among the world's worst documented aflatoxicosis events, with over 300 cases and 125 deaths. Aflatoxin contamination remains a recurring food safety challenge in Kenya and East Africa.

laws.title: Kenya Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act
laws.subtitle: Kenya's wildlife protection critical but companion animal law outdated
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act (Cap. 360) is the primary companion animal welfare law, but like many East African nations, it retains colonial-era structures with limited penalties. Kenya's strength in animal protection is wildlife law — the Wildlife Conservation and Management Act 2013 provides significant protections for Kenya's iconic wildlife (elephants, lions, rhinos). Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) actively fights poaching, including the famous ivory burning events. Wildlife crimes carry serious penalties. The Kenya SPCA operates shelters and advocates for stronger companion animal law reform. Working donkeys and horses are addressed by welfare organizations. Kenya's wildlife tourism economy creates strong economic incentives for wildlife protection.
laws.penalty: Wildlife violations: up to 10 years imprisonment and KES 10 million fine; cruelty to animals (Cap. 360): outdated minimal fines
exceptions: Livestock farming under veterinary standards
Licensed wildlife research
Traditional Maasai and other cattle practices
Community conservancy management
laws.sourceLabel: Kenya Wildlife Conservation and Management Act 2013

quiz.q: What spectacular symbolic act has Kenya used to demonstrate commitment to wildlife protection?
options: Building the world's largest wildlife hospital
Creating the world's largest wildlife sanctuary
quiz.explanation: Kenya has conducted famous public burnings of confiscated ivory stockpiles — a dramatic symbolic demonstration of anti-poaching commitment. The acts, including President Kenyatta's 2016 burning of 105 tons of ivory worth $150 million, sent a powerful global message against the ivory trade.

laws.title: Kenya Marriage Act 2014 — Unified Marriage Law with Polygamy
laws.subtitle: Kenya's 2014 Act unified multiple marriage systems including polygamy
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Marriage Act (2014) was a landmark — it unified multiple separate marriage laws (Christian, civil, Islamic, Hindu, customary) into one Act. The 2014 Act recognizes 5 forms of marriage: Christian, civil, customary, Islamic, and Hindu. Notably, the Act explicitly recognizes polygamous marriages — men can take additional wives without notifying the existing wife. This provision caused significant controversy with women's rights groups. The Act requires registration of all marriages. Kenya's constitution (2010) defines marriage as between a man and a woman. Same-sex relationships are criminalized. Child marriage: minimum age is 18. Kenya has the Matrimonial Property Act 2013 establishing equal rights to matrimonial property. Domestic violence is addressed through the Protection Against Domestic Violence Act 2015.
laws.penalty: Civil family court enforcement; polygamy without consent: civil dispute; domestic violence: criminal penalties up to 30 years for serious cases; child marriage: criminal offense
exceptions: Islamic marriage allows polygamy under Islamic law within the unified Act
Customary law marriages may have different dissolution procedures
Bride price (lobola/ruracio) practices recognized

quiz.q: What controversial polygamy provision did Kenya's 2014 Marriage Act include?
options: Men can take additional wives without notifying existing wives — a controversial provision
Women can also have multiple husbands
quiz.explanation: Kenya's 2014 Marriage Act — despite being a modernizing reform — explicitly recognized that men can take additional wives without prior notification or consent of existing wives. Women's rights groups strongly opposed this provision, arguing it undermined marital equality. The clause reflected a compromise with cultural and religious communities that practice polygamy.

laws.title: Kenya Land Act & National Land Commission
laws.subtitle: 2010 constitution land reform and registration
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's 2010 Constitution (Article 60) established principles of equitable land access and eliminated gender discrimination in land rights. The National Land Commission Act (2012) and Land Act (2012) implemented these principles, creating the National Land Commission (NLC) to manage public land and address historical injustices. The Land Registration Act (2012) consolidated and replaced colonial-era statutes. Kenya uses a system of freehold and leasehold titles. Community land (recognized under the Community Land Act 2016) protects rights of indigenous communities. The coast region has significant historical land injustice from colonial-era 'ten-mile coastal strip' arrangements.
laws.penalty: Illegal land grabbing: criminal prosecution; NLC historical injustice recommendations: government action required
exceptions: Women's equal land rights guaranteed under 2010 Constitution
Community Land Act 2016 protects indigenous territorial rights
laws.source: Land Act 2012; Land Registration Act 2012; Community Land Act 2016

quiz.q: What significant gender equality change did Kenya's 2010 Constitution make regarding land rights?
options: Required 50% of all land to be owned by women
Eliminated gender discrimination in land rights
Allowed women to own land only through cooperatives
Required husband's consent for women's land purchases
quiz.explanation: Kenya's 2010 Constitution Article 60 established that land shall be held, used, and managed equitably and efficiently, explicitly prohibiting gender discrimination in access to land — a major reform in a country where customary law had severely restricted women's land rights.

laws.title: Kenya Consumer Protection Act 2012
laws.subtitle: Consumer rights with Competition Authority enforcement
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Consumer Protection Act (2012) consolidated consumer rights including protection from unfair trade practices, product safety, and information rights. The Competition Authority of Kenya (CAK) enforces both competition and consumer protection law. The CAK has been active against pyramid schemes, misleading M-Pesa promotions, and fuel price manipulation. Kenya's Central Bank Consumer Protection Regulations cover mobile banking consumers — critical given M-Pesa's near-universal usage. The Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS) handles product safety certification. Kenya's consumer protection has a particular focus on informal market consumers who represent the majority of economic activity.
laws.penalty: CAK fine: up to KES 10 million or 10% of turnover; pyramid scheme: criminal prosecution up to 5 years
exceptions: CAK enforces both competition and consumer protection
Mobile money (M-Pesa) consumer protection regulated by Central Bank

quiz.q: Which institution enforces Kenya's Consumer Protection Act?
quiz.explanation: The Competition Authority of Kenya (CAK) enforces the Consumer Protection Act 2012 alongside competition law.

laws.title: Constitution of Kenya 2010
laws.subtitle: Devolution and progressive rights
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's 2010 Constitution transformed the country's governance structure, introducing a devolved system of 47 counties, a bicameral legislature (National Assembly and Senate), and an independent judiciary. Chapter 4 contains an extensive Bill of Rights. The constitution was seen as a major reform following the 2007–2008 post-election violence that killed 1,300. The Supreme Court under Chief Justice David Maraga controversially nullified the 2017 presidential election—the first time in Africa a sitting president was ordered to stand for re-election.
laws.penalty: Constitutional violations adjudicated by the Supreme Court; government accountability mechanisms
exceptions: Emergency provisions under Article 58
Limitation of rights clause for national security

quiz.q: How many counties does Kenya's devolved system have under the 2010 Constitution?
quiz.explanation: Kenya's 2010 Constitution established 47 counties as part of its devolved system of government, replacing the previous centralized structure.

laws.title: Same-Sex Criminalization / Penal Code Sections 162-165
laws.subtitle: Colonial-era anti-LGBTQ+ laws
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Penal Code Sections 162–165, inherited from British colonial law, criminalize 'carnal knowledge against the order of nature' with up to 14 years imprisonment. In 2019, the High Court upheld these provisions, rejecting a petition by LGBTQ+ rights groups. A subsequent 2023 Supreme Court ruling allowed LGBTQ+ organizations to register as associations, creating a partial legal contradiction. Anti-LGBTQ+ sentiment is widespread across religious and political communities.
laws.penalty: Up to 14 years imprisonment for same-sex acts
exceptions: No legal exceptions provided
Registration of advocacy organizations now permitted

quiz.q: What was the outcome of the 2019 High Court ruling on Kenya's anti-LGBTQ+ laws?
options: The court struck down the laws
The court created a partial exemption
quiz.explanation: In 2019, Kenya's High Court upheld Sections 162-165 of the Penal Code, rejecting petitions to decriminalize same-sex relationships, though the Supreme Court later allowed LGBTQ+ organizations to register.

laws.title: M-Pesa and Mobile Money Regulation
laws.subtitle: Central Bank of Kenya / mobile finance
laws.fullDescription: Kenya is the global pioneer of mobile money, with M-Pesa (launched 2007 by Safaricom) processing over 60% of Kenya's GDP in transactions. The Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) regulates mobile money under the National Payment System Act. Kenya's fintech ecosystem—including mobile loans (Fuliza, M-Shwari), insurance, and digital credit—has transformed financial inclusion but raised concerns about over-indebtedness and predatory lending through unregulated digital credit apps.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for unlicensed payment services; CBK administrative sanctions
exceptions: Agent banking has separate lighter regulations
Microfinance institutions have modified requirements

quiz.q: Approximately what percentage of Kenya's GDP does M-Pesa process in transactions?
quiz.explanation: M-Pesa processes over 60% of Kenya's GDP in transactions, making Kenya the world's most advanced mobile money economy.

laws.title: Plastic Bag Ban / Environmental Management
laws.subtitle: Kenya's world-leading plastic ban
laws.fullDescription: Kenya implemented one of the world's strictest plastic bag bans in 2017, with penalties of up to 4 years imprisonment or KSh 4 million fines for manufacturing, selling, or using plastic bags. Kenya is also vulnerable to climate change effects—droughts, floods, and erratic rainfall affecting food security. The government pushed for a global plastics treaty at UN negotiations, and Kenya hosts UNEP headquarters in Nairobi.
laws.penalty: Up to 4 years imprisonment or KSh 4 million fine for plastic bag violations
exceptions: Industrial packaging with special permits
Medical uses exempt

quiz.q: What is the maximum imprisonment for violating Kenya's plastic bag ban?
quiz.explanation: Kenya's 2017 plastic bag ban imposes penalties of up to 4 years imprisonment or KSh 4 million in fines, making it one of the world's strictest such regulations.

laws.title: 2017 Election Nullification / IEBC
laws.subtitle: Supreme Court annulment of presidential election
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Supreme Court made global headlines in September 2017 by nullifying the re-election of President Uhuru Kenyatta, citing irregularities in the transmission of results by the IEBC (Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission). It was only the second time in African history a presidential election was annulled. The opposition under Raila Odinga subsequently boycotted the repeat election. Subsequent reforms to IEBC have been contested.
laws.penalty: Electoral offenses: up to 5 years imprisonment; candidates can be barred
exceptions: IEBC commissioners have qualified immunity for good-faith decisions
Political party decisions handled separately

quiz.q: What made Kenya's 2017 Supreme Court ruling historically significant for Africa?
options: First time a leader was imprisoned for election fraud
Only the second time in Africa a presidential election had been nullified
First time opposition boycotted an election
First time electronic voting was ruled invalid
quiz.explanation: Kenya's Supreme Court nullification of Uhuru Kenyatta's 2017 re-election was only the second time in African history that a presidential election result had been annulled by a court.

laws.title: Anti-Terrorism Law / Al-Shabaab
laws.subtitle: Counter-terrorism and security operations
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Prevention of Terrorism Act 2012 and subsequent amendments target the threat from Al-Shabaab, the Somalia-based jihadist group responsible for the 2013 Westgate Mall attack (67 killed), 2015 Garissa University attack (148 killed), and numerous smaller attacks. Kenya's participation in AMISOM in Somalia brings retaliatory attacks. The security services have been accused of extrajudicial killings and enforced disappearances of terrorism suspects.
laws.penalty: Life imprisonment for terrorism; death penalty in capital terrorism cases
exceptions: Cooperation with authorities reduces sentences
Surrender and rehabilitation programs for low-level members

quiz.q: How many people were killed in the 2015 Al-Shabaab attack on Garissa University?
quiz.explanation: The Al-Shabaab attack on Garissa University College in April 2015 killed 148 people, making it the deadliest attack in Kenya since the 1998 US Embassy bombing.

laws.title: National Land Commission Act 2012
laws.subtitle: Land reform and historical injustices
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's National Land Commission, established by the 2010 Constitution, addresses historical land injustices including colonial-era dispossessions and post-independence allocations to political elites. Land conflicts are a root cause of Kenya's recurrent election violence—communities in the Rift Valley, Coast, and Mount Elgon have competing historical claims. The Community Land Act 2016 recognizes communal land rights.
laws.penalty: Land grabbing criminal offense; courts can reverse illegal allocations
exceptions: Customary land rights protected for community lands
Squatter rights after long occupation recognized in some cases

quiz.q: What legislation recognizes communal land rights in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: The Community Land Act 2016 recognizes and protects the community land rights of communities that historically occupied land under customary tenure in Kenya.

laws.title: Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act 2018
laws.subtitle: Digital rights and cyber regulation
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act 2018 has been criticized for its overbroad provisions on cyberbullying, publication of false information, and computer fraud, which have been used against journalists and bloggers. In 2023, Kenya began implementing the Data Protection Act 2019, which established the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner. Kenya is also home to Silicon Savannah—major tech companies including Huawei, Microsoft, and Google have offices in Nairobi.
laws.penalty: Up to 10 years imprisonment for computer fraud; fines up to KSh 5 million
exceptions: Public interest defense in journalism provisions
Security research exemptions
laws.sourceLabel: Kenya Office of Data Protection Commissioner

quiz.q: What is the informal name for Nairobi's technology and startup hub?
quiz.explanation: 'Silicon Savannah' is the informal name for Nairobi's growing technology and startup ecosystem, playing on Silicon Valley and Kenya's savannah landscape.

laws.title: Two-Thirds Gender Rule
laws.subtitle: Constitutional gender representation
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's 2010 Constitution mandates that no more than two-thirds of elected or appointed government positions should be of the same gender (Article 81(b) and Article 27(8)). Despite this, Kenya has consistently failed to implement the rule—Parliament has repeatedly failed to pass legislation to enforce it, and the Supreme Court has declined to dissolve Parliament over the failure. Women currently hold about 23% of parliamentary seats.
laws.penalty: Constitutional violation in appointments; courts may order corrective measures
exceptions: Transitional provisions for phased implementation
Elective positions cannot be mandated the same way as appointed ones

quiz.q: What fraction of elected or appointed positions must the minority gender hold under Kenya's constitution?
quiz.explanation: Kenya's 2010 Constitution mandates that no more than two-thirds of any elective or appointive body should be of the same gender, guaranteeing at least one-third representation for the minority gender.

laws.title: Universal Health Coverage / SHA
laws.subtitle: Social Health Authority and UHC
laws.fullDescription: President Ruto's administration launched the Social Health Authority (SHA) in 2023, replacing the National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) as part of an ambitious Universal Health Coverage program. The mandatory SHA levy (2.75% of gross income) faced court challenges and implementation difficulties. Kenya also battles recurring health crises: cholera, malaria, and the HIV epidemic (1.5 million people living with HIV). Maternal mortality remains high in rural areas.
laws.penalty: Penalties for employers not remitting SHA contributions; fraud in claims
exceptions: Informal sector contributions at flat rate
Indigent population registered by counties

quiz.q: What percentage of gross income is the mandatory Social Health Authority (SHA) levy in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: Kenya's Social Health Authority requires a mandatory levy of 2.75% of gross income from formal sector workers to fund Universal Health Coverage.

laws.title: Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission
laws.subtitle: EACC and Chapter 6 leadership integrity
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) enforces Chapter 6 of the 2010 Constitution, which sets integrity standards for public officers. Politicians must declare wealth, and those with corruption convictions are barred from office. Despite this, Kenya consistently ranks in the bottom half of Transparency International's index. High-profile corruption scandals—including the Kenya Power scandal, NYS fraud, and the 2018 Arror/Kimwarer dam scandal—involve billions in stolen funds.
laws.penalty: Forfeiture of office; criminal prosecution; fines; imprisonment
exceptions: Plea bargaining provisions
Protected whistleblower status for informants

quiz.q: Which chapter of Kenya's 2010 Constitution establishes leadership integrity requirements?
quiz.explanation: Chapter 6 of Kenya's 2010 Constitution establishes the National Values and Principles of Governance and sets integrity and ethics standards for all public officers.

laws.title: Nairobi as East Africa Hub / EAC
laws.subtitle: East African Community trade integration
laws.fullDescription: Kenya is the dominant economy in the East African Community (EAC), which includes Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan, and the DRC. Nairobi serves as the regional hub for multinational corporations operating in East Africa. The EAC has a common external tariff but faces non-tariff barriers, border delays, and NTBs. Kenya's port of Mombasa handles most of landlocked East Africa's imports.
laws.penalty: Customs violations prosecuted under East African Community Customs Management Act
exceptions: EAC Common External Tariff exceptions for sensitive goods
Special Economic Zones with modified tariff rules

quiz.q: Which port serves as the main import gateway for landlocked East African countries?
quiz.explanation: Kenya's Port of Mombasa is the primary gateway for imports destined for landlocked East African countries including Uganda, Rwanda, and parts of DRC.

laws.title: Employment Act 2007 / Informal Economy
laws.subtitle: Worker rights in Kenya's jua kali sector
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Employment Act 2007 provides statutory rights including minimum wage, maternity/paternity leave, and protection against unfair dismissal. However, 80%+ of Kenyan workers are in the informal sector (known as jua kali—'hot sun' in Swahili). The government introduced the Affordable Housing Levy (1.5% of gross salary) in 2023 as part of President Ruto's housing agenda, which faced court challenges before being upheld.
laws.penalty: Fines and civil claims for employment law violations; labor court awards
exceptions: Domestic workers have modified provisions
Agricultural workers have seasonal employment rules
laws.sourceLabel: Kenya Ministry of Labour Employment Act

quiz.q: What does the Swahili term 'jua kali' mean in the context of Kenya's informal economy?
options: Hot sun (informal workers who work outdoors)
quiz.explanation: 'Jua kali' literally means 'hot sun' in Swahili and refers to Kenya's informal economy workers—artisans, mechanics, traders—who traditionally worked outdoors under the hot sun.

laws.title: Media Council Act 2013 / Press Freedom
laws.subtitle: Media regulation and journalist safety
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Media Council Act 2013 established a statutory media regulator. Despite constitutional protections for free expression and a relatively vibrant press, journalists face threats including physical violence, arrest under the Computer Misuse Act, and economic pressure on media houses. The arrest of bloggers and social media critics accelerated under the Finance Bill protests of 2024, when Gen Z-led protests stormed Parliament and at least 50 protesters were killed.
laws.penalty: Criminal defamation: fines; computer misuse violations: imprisonment
exceptions: Parliamentary privilege for statements in the House
Fair comment and public interest defenses

quiz.q: In 2024, Kenyan protesters stormed which building during Finance Bill protests?
quiz.explanation: In June 2024, Gen Z-led protesters opposing the Finance Bill 2024 stormed and briefly occupied Kenya's Parliament building, with security forces killing at least 50 protesters.

laws.title: Wildlife Conservation and Management Act 2013
laws.subtitle: KWS and elephant/rhino protection
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Wildlife Conservation and Management Act 2013 gives the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) authority to protect wildlife and manage national parks. Kenya has successfully grown its elephant and rhino populations through strict anti-poaching enforcement. Ivory and rhino horn trading are strictly banned. Human-wildlife conflict is a major issue—elephants raid farms, lions kill livestock—with compensation mechanisms often inadequate for affected communities.
laws.penalty: Up to life imprisonment for killing endangered species like elephants and rhinos
exceptions: Problem animal control by KWS officers
Scientific research with permits

quiz.q: What is the maximum penalty for killing an elephant or rhino in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: Kenya's Wildlife Conservation and Management Act 2013 provides for up to life imprisonment for killing elephants, rhinos, and other endangered species.

laws.title: Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) Reform
laws.subtitle: Education reform controversy
laws.fullDescription: Kenya's Competency Based Curriculum (CBC), introduced in 2017 to replace the 8-4-4 system, has been highly controversial. It restructures schooling into 2-6-3-3-3 (pre-primary, lower primary, upper primary, junior secondary, senior secondary). Critics including parents and teachers argue the curriculum is too expensive (requiring parents to buy workbooks), confusing, and untested. Junior secondary school (Grade 7-9) teachers are in dispute over deployment and pay.
laws.penalty: Sanctions for schools not implementing approved curriculum
exceptions: Special needs schools have modified curriculum approaches
International schools follow recognized international curricula
laws.sourceLabel: Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development CBC

quiz.q: What is the grade structure under Kenya's Competency Based Curriculum (CBC)?
quiz.explanation: Kenya's CBC restructures education into a 2-6-3-3-3 system: 2 years pre-primary, 6 years lower primary, 3 years upper primary, 3 years junior secondary, and 3 years senior secondary.

laws.title: Refugees Act 2021 / Somali Refugee Policy
laws.subtitle: Dadaab and refugee protection
laws.fullDescription: Kenya hosts over 500,000 refugees, primarily Somalis in Dadaab camp (one of the world's largest) and South Sudanese in Kakuma. The Refugees Act 2021 moved toward a more rights-based framework but Kenya has periodically threatened to close Dadaab, citing security concerns after Al-Shabaab attacks. The Kenyan government's encampment policy restricts refugees from living and working freely in urban areas.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for illegal entry; refugees violating encampment policy face detention
exceptions: Asylum seekers have right to registration
Urban refugees may receive movement permits in some circumstances

quiz.q: Which camp is one of the world's largest refugee camps, hosting primarily Somali refugees in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: Dadaab refugee complex in northeastern Kenya is one of the world's largest refugee camps, hosting primarily Somali refugees who have fled conflict and famine since the early 1990s.

laws.title: HIV/AIDS Prevention and Control Act 2006
laws.subtitle: Kenya's HIV epidemic and PEPFAR
laws.fullDescription: Kenya has one of sub-Saharan Africa's largest HIV epidemics, with approximately 1.5 million people living with HIV. The HIV and AIDS Prevention and Control Act 2006 protects the rights of people living with HIV. Kenya benefits enormously from PEPFAR (US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief), which funds over 70% of HIV treatment. US threats to withdraw PEPFAR funding in 2025 created alarm in Kenya's health system.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for willful transmission of HIV; discrimination against PLHIV prohibited
exceptions: Healthcare workers have reporting obligations
Research and public health interventions

quiz.q: Approximately what percentage of Kenya's HIV treatment funding comes from PEPFAR?
quiz.explanation: Kenya's HIV treatment program is approximately 70% funded by PEPFAR (US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief), making it highly vulnerable to changes in US foreign aid policy.

laws.title: Kenya Revenue Authority / Finance Act
laws.subtitle: Tax reforms and Gen Z protests
laws.fullDescription: Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) implements tax law. The Finance Act 2023 introduced a Housing Levy (1.5%), increased VAT on several items, and introduced new digital service taxes. The Finance Bill 2024 proposed additional taxes including a VAT on bread and cooking oil, which triggered massive Gen Z-led protests in June 2024—the most significant civil unrest in Kenya since 2007–08. President Ruto withdrew the bill after Parliament was stormed.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion: fines and imprisonment; KRA can garnish bank accounts
exceptions: Exempt supplies include basic food items (when not taxed)
Export zero-rating

quiz.q: Why did President Ruto withdraw Kenya's Finance Bill 2024?
options: It was ruled unconstitutional by the Supreme Court
Massive Gen Z-led protests stormed Parliament and demanded withdrawal
quiz.explanation: President Ruto withdrew the Finance Bill 2024 following massive Gen Z-led protests in June 2024, during which demonstrators stormed Parliament and security forces killed at least 50 protesters.

laws.title: Oil Discovery / Petroleum (Exploration) Act
laws.subtitle: Turkana oil and resource governance
laws.fullDescription: Kenya discovered oil in Turkana County in 2012, with Tullow Oil leading exploration. Early oil exports began in 2019 under a pilot program. However, full commercial production has been delayed by infrastructure challenges, low global oil prices, and community protests in Turkana over revenue sharing and employment. Kenya's Petroleum Act 2019 governs upstream operations, with provisions for local content and community development levies.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for illegal petroleum extraction; regulatory sanctions for permit violations
exceptions: Artisanal gas extraction has informal frameworks
Natural gas for cooking has social pricing rules

quiz.q: In which year did Kenya make its significant oil discovery in Turkana County?
quiz.explanation: Kenya discovered oil in Turkana County in 2012, with Tullow Oil leading the exploration that identified commercially viable reserves.
